TITLE: Open Perimeter | Open Data
MATERIALS & TOOLS: Ecoacoustic recordings via iPhone Voice Memo. Visual field recordings via cyanotypes and Camera app. Sound design in Audacity. Data Commons via OpenStreetMap.org. Compiled in After Effects, with minimal help from Claude Code. Two aerial images sources via unnamed photographer from Marinas.com and repost on Pintrest.
RATIONALE (meaning/stakes): Life and its things come and go. If we listen and stay, what can we learn about place, people, and belonging? This ecoacoustic piece considers how landscapes hold openings, personal histories, grief, ritual, and everyday life all at once. Its made from a heart-shaped harbor in southeastern Massachusetts, viewable from my window. My family has lived by it for generations. My mom's memorial was held at the town marina on its edge and her ashes are part of it's tide.
PROJECT DESCRIPTION (mechanics/experienc: An ambient audiovisual composition centered on Scituate Harbor, Massachusetts. The runtime, 4:01.22, spells out the date my mom's ashes entered the harbor tide: April 1, 2022. It's a shifting audio portrait of a harbor with an open perimeter, always letting water in and out, and of memory doing the same thing.

TITLE: Ethical AI: Intimacy as Infrastructure
MATERIALS & TOOLS: Custom built Small Language Model AI via AutoLume, hand-made crystal & metal mobile, TouchDesigner, OSC, projection. AI Model Card available here.
RATIONALE (meaning/stakes): This work explores the inverse of choices made by Big Tech; what is ethical AI, and how can machine learning be reimagined, not just adopted or refused? What might it look like if provencance aligns to public interest rather than profit, if AI is local-only and therefore isn't a climate risk? What is machine learning when the training materials are emotional and pre-literate rather than text-centric, personal and bestowed rather than non-consensually extracted, if the process by which the corpus is collected and trained is is slow and initmate, engagment is embodied rather than chatted, and care and safety replace the erosion of trust and confusion of reality? What are machines, what is learning, what is articifical and what is the real that we want? What does modelling good look like?
PROJECT DESCRIPTION (mechanics/experienc: A compact AI was trained on a collection of roughly 500 deeply personal items bestowed (rather than extracted) using AutoLume. Its responses are projected through a three-foot crystal-and-metal mobile, serving as a real-world metaphor for how machine learning develops via corpus, training, and predictive, prismatic, shifting recombination. Viewers interact with the piece through facial expressions and full-body movements via OSC, which influence the AI’s behavior in real time. The interactions are orchestrated in TouchDesigner and communicated through a Local Area Network, making the experience fully offline and self-contained.
PRESENTED WHERE & WHEN: Presented December 2025 at City University of New York, Hunter College Goldberg Studio Space, NYC, NY.

TITLE: Latent Curricula: Computational Tiny Prints
MATERIALS & TOOLS: In-progress. Found and shared 'love curriculum' experiments in Cavalry / Typeflow / Typeface Animator.
RATIONALE (meaning/stakes): If the universe is the syllabus, how do we study love as liberation? Drawn from encounters with songs, texts, streets, and dialogue, these curricular fragments bend at the edge of legibility. What is learning, and how does it interact with art? Printmaking has long fueled social action; when small-scale and personal tiny prints mix with technology, what new scales of reach, participation, and impact become possible?
PROJECT DESCRIPTION (mechanics/experienc: Over a few days I noted encounters that might serve as curricula for radical love, the idea that love (beyond romantic or familial love) is important in places where it historically been sidelined or avoided, such as in classrooms, workplaces, politics, and beyond. The snippets I collected -- lyrics to Prince's I Would Die For You, a photo of a stickie note posted in the Union Square subway after Trump's first presidential election, an excerpt from an overheard conversation, an excerpt from an interview with Ian McKellen, a quote from Dr. Cornel West -- are reimagined as digital tiny prints: little messages and protests to share.

TITLE: Soft Machine (Title after Burroughs)
MATERIALS & TOOLS: Guided performance art. Group phone flashlights, iPhone webcam on center table tracks group light input, sends via Bluetooth to TouchDesigner, custom TouchDesigner patch handles real-time light detection and video triggering, outputs to projection, developed with help from Claude Code. Original video is self-recorded night footage from the Maine coast, shot near amusement rides. Live voice performance by Reardon.
RATIONALE (meaning/stakes): A performance about bodies and machines, and the uneasy balance between human vitality and machine logic. Using light as indicator and medium, it constructs a space where participation is both an act of belonging and a form of control. It asks not whether we are part of the machine, but what kind of system we are becoming together.
PROJECT DESCRIPTION (mechanics/experienc: A group stands in a circle around a webcam on a low pedestal. The camera reads the light participants contorl and collect via their mobile phone flashlight. When enough light points at the lens, a video comes into focus: abstract light patterns recorded at night of amusement rides near beach in Maine. When the light drops, the video falls apart. A voice guides the group toward the center, asks for their light, and lets them decide whether to keep it raised or let it drop. The voice speaks of indicator lights, the small signals machines use to say they're working, that they read you. It speaks of machines as relationships to power, to control, of who shapes whom. It says no one here is just input. It closes by asking what kind of systems we are and want to become together.
PRESENTED WHERE & WHEN: Presented June 20, 2026 at City University of New York, Hunter College Blackbox Theater, NYC, NY.

TITLE: Time & Light
MATERIALS & TOOLS: Cyanotype on 4"x4" bisqueware tiles, sealed with spray quartz. Custom-built computer vision web app, coded in collaboration with Claude Code.
RATIONALE (meaning/stakes): What does it mean to tend, not control, and to be alive, and then remembered? Plants grow from cuttings, carrying the shape of where they came from. This work follows that idea through the women in my family: my grandmother's garden and her sisters in law's, widening out to my mom and her sister, and now held by me and my sister, at the house where I cared for my mom until she died. Care moves in both directions, passed down like a garden. A cyanotype holds a real trace of a plant using only sunlight, an imprint left behind. It's the same question I keep asking in my work with technology: can a system tend, rather than control, the people it touches?
PROJECT DESCRIPTION (mechanics/experienc: Cyanotype portraits of a garden passed through the women in my family, installed as tiles at the entryway between the garden and the home, bringing the outside in and turning something seasonal into something permanent. The piece grew out of an experimental darkroom practice, feminine craft worked alongside digital tools: a phone reads the cyanotype's blue through its camera, treating each analog print as an image in its own right, and triggers a matching set of looping GIFs, hybrid analog and digital portraits built from archival photos of the four women who make up my core family, my grandmother, my mom, her sister, my sister, and me. The piece pairs a fixed, sun-printed record with a living, camera-triggered one, a system built to hold and to love, rather than to watch or take.

TITLE: Re-threaded
MATERIALS & TOOLS: Dance, custom-made sonic loops, live breathwork, live projected colored-oil backdrops.
RATIONALE (meaning/stakes): Re-threaded is a performance installation that explores the most foundational embodied technology we have: breath. Taking breathing seriously as part of choreography, we delve into the ways that breathwork can help us move through the temporal and spatial landscapes integral to the stories we tell with our bodies.
PROJECT DESCRIPTION (mechanics/experienc: This performance installation draws movement vocabulary from a piece for which OreOluwa Badaki was part of the choreographic team, called Threaded, which premiered at Philadelphia Fringe Fest in the Fall of 2025. Threaded used choreographic phrasing and formations that wove together shapes that have represented time in different cultures -- (e.g. ouroboros, sacred spiral, lemiscate, etc.). We build on this vocabulary as an invitation for performers and participants to consider the role of breath in moving through time. Performers and participants are invited to consider what shapes time takes for them, and how breath can help them move through and with these shapes. The original Threaded piece was solely a dance performance, this performance installation integrates oil projects and sonic looping (curated by Lucius Von Joo, Chris Moffett, and Emily Reardon) to visualize, physicalize, and expand the the ways that breath moves through the piece and invite performers and participants to travel through time in new ways.

TITLE: Research for Humans
MATERIALS & TOOLS: Local, open-weight AI: OLMo 3 7B from the Allen Institute, run entirely on-device via Ollama with retrieval-augmented generation over a custom corpus of all 7,463 open-access ISLS papers. Pipeline built in collaboration with Claude Code. The automaton's body is an e-waste label maker housed in a recycled suitcase and covered by a recycled cape, with a custom 3D-printed head lit by Adafruit-controlled lights, an e-waste iPhone as its screen, and an external keyboard for input. Each question returns two prints, one to wear and one added to the installation. AI Model Card available here.
RATIONALE (meaning/stakes): The world is in crisis, but there is malleability in the crumble. Trust in institutions, expertise, and each other is eroding at the exact moment we need science and research most. This piece treats that as a relationship problem, not a technology problem, reclaiming AI as a possible repair for academic trust rather than the force breaking it. A single, open corpus runs entirely on a local, open model, so everything it offers traces back to a paper anyone could read themselves. It asks what research could become if it circulated rather than accumulated, if it were carried and worn rather than filed away.
PROJECT DESCRIPTION (mechanics/experienc: A visitor approaches an automaton and types in a question, the kind of encounter you'd expect from a fortune telling machine that stops passersby, not a search bar. It searches a an elite corpus of learning science research, work a community fought to free from the paywalls and gatekeeping of academia, and generates a reply grounded in what it finds there, more provocation than closed answer. The response prints twice as small label stickers. One goes to the visitor to wear, meant to start a conversation. The other joins the automaton's running record, so each response becomes part of what the next visitor encounters.

TITLE: Sesame Street Family Play
MATERIALS & TOOLS: iPhone & Android App for Caretakers of Young Kids
RATIONALE (meaning/stakes): How might we leverage parents’ everyday phone use to promote off-screen family connection and address the persistent challenges of daily caregiving—such as tooth-brushing, waiting in line, or bedtime—when emotional intensity is common? In what ways might play function as an intervention to help parents reduce reliance on screens while strengthening their capacity for self-regulation and responsive caregiving?
PROJECT DESCRIPTION (mechanics/experienc: Kids and grown ups play off-screen games together. Game ideas and rules are generated by the grown up on their phone, based on current setting (from in the tubby, to at the dentist, to at a restaurant, to waiting at a bus stop), number of players, and available props. Grown ups deliver the game in real time—through voice, props, and imagination—not devices. Games transform “have to” moments into shared joy, strengthening bonds. As grown-ups gain confidence in creating play, they rely less on the app and more on their own spontaneity.
PRESENTED BY & ROLE: Responsible for: Concepting, pitching, play experience & system design, play research. Phone app built on 3rd party game engine.

TITLE: Grover's Block Party
MATERIALS & TOOLS: Analog-Digital Hybrid, Traditional Playthings, Augmented Reality
RATIONALE (meaning/stakes): Young children’s deep, imaginative play with traditional toys—like blocks—builds critical skills, but screens often pull them away. How might we harness kids’ attraction to technology to restore the rich benefits of deep play, make foundational literacy more engaging, and shift tech’s role from directing play to following the child’s lead—deepening engagement and fostering learning?
PROJECT DESCRIPTION (mechanics/experienc:
Kids play with letter blocks on a playdate with Grover & 26 Letter Muppets. Grover & letter Muppets react to child-led play -- noticing, commenting, questioning, singing, serving up letter videos, & more, to scaffold experimentation & deepen learning. 

Computer vision ‘watches’. Dynamic ‘mood’ tagging automatically animates Grover. Augmented reality enables Grover & letter Muppets to scaffold player. Adaptive personalized patterns & scaffolds drawn from learning science grow with kids play. 

Formative research included iterative in-house play sessions to define a taxonomy of play patterns (pictured here). Summative research included providing families with these sets as well as non-AR off the shelf block sets, pre/post focus groups, Dscout video recordings matched to behavioral data coded together.
PRESENTED BY & ROLE: Responsible for: Entire project, including concepting, pitching, system design, technology innovation lead, excluding 3rd party vendor and minimal art direction.

TITLE: The Electric Company
MATERIALS & TOOLS: Cross-platform literacy ecosystem including website, TV show, and comic book series
RATIONALE (meaning/stakes): Kids who aren’t reading at grade level by fourth grade often struggle to make the critical shift from learning to read to reading to learn—a turning point strongly tied to long-term academic outcomes. We reimagined The Electric Company as a transmedia literacy experience designed to reach struggling readers ages six to nine where they already were: online and playing games.
PROJECT DESCRIPTION (mechanics/experienc: Kids use the website to play digital games, watch videos, and more. The digital hub and transmedia narrative connects to and from the PBS television series and comicbook set. The unified literacy ecosystem featured artists including Common, Lin-Manuel Miranda, and Reggie Watts.
PRESENTED BY & ROLE: Responsible for: Directed the experience design— shaping narrative and play-based active learning while producing the technical specifications, logic flows, wireframes, and user flows, and leading playtesting with children across the United States. My work on the project received an Emmy Award.
